title: The Longest "10 Minutes" Ever
text:
The Longest "10 Minutes" Ever. After a year, I'm going back to a different coffee maker. This Bunn takes forever to brew a pot of coffee. It's ok if you're one of those very organized people who can remember to set up the Bunn the night before to brew automatically before you wake up, but for people like me, who stumble to the coffee pot in the morning and need some as quickly as possible, it's a pain.

The Phase Brew takes so long because it heats all the water up to the right temp before sending any of it through the coffee grounds, but, honestly, while that all sounds good, I can't tell one bit of difference between all the water being heated up first, and any other coffee pot that simply sends the water through as it is heating. I think it's just a gimmick and a selling point that actually means very little for the consumer.

Another problem is that the "clean" indicator, that tells when the maker needs to be cleaned, goes off all the time. As other long-term users review this brewer, you'll see that this happens a lot, and Bunn claims it's because of local power grids. Well, I don't have any control over the local power grid, so I can only exercise what control I do have by buying a reasonably-priced brewer that actually works when I need it to work.

****Update as of 6/30/13****

I eventually returned this unit to Bunn after they agreed that there was a defect with the cleaning indicator, and they sent a replacement very quickly. Customer service was terrific, but the replacement had the same problem as the first model. If I'd been diligent and called them again, I'm sure they would have sent another replacement, but I'm not diligent. I'm a lazy internet shopper, and it was easier to just buy a tried & true workhorse brand brewer for every day use and use the French press for something special occasions.
